ranked_facts.concept_key: enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature
ranked_facts.why: The presence of an enlarged cardiac silhouette with increased pulmonary vasculature is more consistent with left heart obstructive lesions, such as hypoplastic left heart syndrome, which would lead to increased pulmonary blood flow and cardiomegaly, whereas non-cardiac causes would not typically present with these specific cardiac findings.

ranked_facts.concept_key: loud single S2 with bounding pulses and wide pulse pressure
ranked_facts.why: A loud single S2 with bounding pulses and wide pulse pressure is indicative of a patent ductus arteriosus or other cardiac anomalies that lead to a significant left-to-right shunt, which would be more consistent with other cardiac anomalies, whereas right heart obstructive lesions would typically present with different clinical findings.
